wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create carrying both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=principal_control create carrying only one of the two matches no variant and is denied with zero writes. For purpose=agent_control the immutable accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision is resolved by its whole-value claim of retype(this EventId, realm); the genesis MUST NOT carry a backward agent_provision ref, which would create an EventId cycle. The verifier cross-binds the complete actor/controller AccountIds, PCR delegation and provision payload before materializing Agent status. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch proves its separate accepted organization authority. A self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical semantic_refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact account ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis: a purpose=principal_control ak.realm.create carrying neither executed_by nor authorization_ref. The create carries no DID-inception Event reference, because DID inception is method-native material and not an Arkret Event. Registration-time DID control evidence is the frozen typed principal_registration_anchor carried by the genesis submission: the verifier rebuilds the registration-time DID, terminal version / history head, normalized DID Document and then-active update key from that one anchor, recomputes SHA-256 over its RFC 8785 JCS bytes and requires the result to equal the identity creation control proof registration_anchor_digest. It validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant. The selector only routes to this verifier and proves no authorization: a create that reaches it without the complete ordered genesis unit, anchor and accepted receipt closure is still rejected with zero writes.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical semantic_refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical semantic_refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the root-round responder; glare branch: the full signed request Event author ActorId referenced by requests[0], never the Station receipt issuer_id; requests MUST be strictly ascending by the complete request_event_ref wire string UTF-8 unsigned bytes, with duplicate Event refs rejected regardless of receipt digest and no receiver-side sorting or deduplication), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.sidecar_account_self_authored_proof: Admitted only when Event actor_id is the account branch and its complete AccountId is the authenticated controller account. The reducer derives controller_account_id byte-for-byte from actor_id.account_id, uses (realm_id, controller_account_id) as the singleton key, and rejects the service actor branch with sidecar_create_denied before revealing existence. The same exact AccountId binds Sidecar membership, MLS genesis and participant authority; principal-only equality is forbidden.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field to be present, and top_level_fields_absent requires every listed field to be absent, evaluated member by member. A member that is present with a null value still counts as present and is still subject to that member's own schema, so top_level_fields_absent is not a 'not both present' selector; the two field selectors MUST NOT appear in one when object. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.semantic_refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry and resolve to exactly one closed payload schema.
An accepted durable Event becomes shared history only when the current authority includes its exact bytes in a signed RealmCommit for the Event's own Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream.
Stream identity is derived from the Event's closed scope. Realm, each Circle, and each Sidecar have independent commit streams; no Realm-global total chain exists.
Event carries no chain predecessor or authority-commit proof. Only RealmCommit carries previous_commit_ref, and only within the same stream.
Reducers derive typed current results by replaying committed Events in stream position order. Account-private material is outside shared authority-commit streams.

wire_scope=durable_event does NOT imply reducer_input=true. A durable Event is one whose exact bytes a RealmCommit can cover; reducer_input=true additionally asserts that replaying this Realm's committed Events suffices to derive the typed current results the kind writes. A kind whose real durable effect is holder-Station private service state -- keyed on material that never enters the Event stream, or on a counterpart mirror that zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 3 forbids from advancing a reducer -- MUST carry reducer_input=false and MUST name the canonical service_contracts row that spells out its branches, durable effect, unique key, prior-state CAS, exact retry and zero-side-effect rejection. Withdrawing Realm typed-result dispatch never withdraws the kind's admission, signature, commit evidence or private transactional effect: the five ak.contact.* kinds are the worked example (ak.contact.admission.v1). Setting reducer_input=false without registering where the effect actually lands is the defect this rule exists to prevent.

result_writes[] is the machine contract for which typed current results one Event kind writes, in what order, and under which closed condition; zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10 read it as the source of truth, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_contracts validates every declared row: a declared value_projection member MUST be declared by that row's value_schema_ref, and a whole-value set MUST write every member that schema requires. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THIS IS A KNOWN GAP: 126 of the 131 reducer_input kinds declare it; the remaining 5 have an explicit durable-fact or authority-commit effect classification and intentionally no typed-current-result row. The declaring kinds are deliberately not enumerated here: event_kinds[] already is that list, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_coverage_note recomputes both counts from the rows. Normative prose MUST NOT cite result_writes[] for a kind that does not declare it. The converse obligation binds a declaring kind: its rows MUST enumerate EVERY typed current result its accepted admission writes on the shared face; atomic multi-family writes land all rows in one batch or none.

Every active persistent kind (durable_event or actor_private_event) MUST carry one closed result_effect_ownership object. A typed_result_writer owns non-empty result_writes[] and no second owner; a private_service_effect names an active service_contracts row whose branches cover that exact actor-private Event kind; a durable_fact_no_current_projection names its normative definition and carries no typed-current-result write; an authority_commit_effect names the structured authority-commit service contract and MUST NOT introduce a second governance counter; an owned_gap is temporary only while it names a live owner_report and exact closure condition. Unknown classifications, unresolved definitions, orphan service branches, shared/private mixing, malformed authority contracts or any classification that contradicts reducer_input/result_writes[] fail tools/artifact_lint:result_effect_ownership.

transition_contracts declares the lifecycle axis of a typed current result family: its closed state set, its entry idiom (exactly one of initial_state / initial_states / template), its terminal states and its allowed (from, to) edges. tools/artifact_lint:fsm_reachability reads it together with every transition result_projection and requires that each declared state be reachable from the entry set, that each allowed edge have a write that can perform it, that no const edge leave the table and that no terminal state carry an outgoing edge. A family that declares a machine MUST NOT be written by any non-transition projection: a set installs a state without passing the table, which would make allowed_transitions documentation rather than a rule. Between the authority-commit clean break and 2026-09-18 this block did not exist while the gate still read it under the removed cell_* names, so check reported success over four normative paragraphs (zh/models/circle.md, zh/models/morph.md, zh/models/realm-and-space.md, zh/models/strand-and-message.md) that name transition_contracts as the source of truth for object lifecycle transitions; an absent or empty block is now a failure. Those four object families are themselves still unregistered, so their archive / restore lifecycle has no machine contract yet -- that is a coverage gap, not a licence to read the prose as satisfied.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Only x_* fields explicitly admitted by a concrete payload schema are non-critical extensions; they are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Current-v1 has no generic Event requirements or critical_extensions carrier. New critical semantics require a new or upgraded registered kind/schema and a complete activation package.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

Agent key authorization is a commit-ordered projection security command with complete explicit revocation set representation. Same-key replacement removes all authorization dots visible at the signed basis and adds one replacement dot, after exact revision and authority checks at execution. Competing replacements cannot survive as concurrent permission heads. Runtime replacement pairs a new raw key and revokes prior active keys in the same confirmed transaction.

models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 needs the directed target of an Invite to be readable from the Invite's own id at every later transition, because the release of the live-target slot has to be checkable against it. This is that record: create-locked, written once from this Event's own payload, never updated and never written by ak.invite.third_party, so a third-party Invite's stored invitee is absent rather than null. models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 makes this slot the single source of truth for directed-invite liveness: occupancy itself means a live directed invite exists, so the slot carries no second state axis. event_kinds.payload: Invite revoke.
